Hi Rafael,

Thanks for the demo earlier — the team appreciated seeing the autoscaling behavior for high-concurrency inferencing. We have two questions we want to close out quickly so we can decide which deployment path to pursue for our POC: Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private VPC.

1) Data at rest: In the Dedicated option, what guarantees do we have that model inputs and generated outputs are purged vs retained? We require a 90-day max retention for PII.
2) Network egress and routing: If we choose Private VPC, can we keep all inference traffic inside our VPC with no egress through Redwood control plane? We also want a short list of the operational steps to connect our ALB to the inference endpoints.

Can you send a short checklist for each and any sample configs? Also loop in your security or solutions engineer if helpful.

Appreciate it — aiming to decide by end of next week.

—Lucy
Security & Compliance lead, Ava Health

Lucy — thanks for the clear questions. Below is a concise breakdown (I'll attach a simple network sketch and an ops checklist in a separate email). If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute follow-up focused on security/ops with our Solutions Architect (Marissa) and your cloud team.

Dedicated (Redwood-managed GPUs)
- Data residency: customer data (requests + responses) are stored on encrypted EBS volumes in the selected region; default retention for request logs is 30 days.
- Purge options: we offer contractual retention customization (30/60/90 days) and immediate purge APIs for eligible enterprise accounts.
- Network: traffic terminates at our managed front-door; TLS 1.3 end-to-end. No VPC peering required.
- Trade-offs: simpler onboarding; slightly higher egress control risk since traffic touches our control plane. Good for customers who prefer low ops overhead.

Private VPC (Customer-hosted control plane or VPC-hosted data path)
- Data residency: you control the subnets and storage; request/response blobs never persist in Redwood-managed storage unless explicitly allowed.
- Purge: you control lifecycle via your storage policies; immediate deletion is possible since data is in customer storage.
- Network: supports private connectivity (VPC peering, PrivateLink, or direct connections). We provide step-by-step ALB->endpoint config and a sidecar to manage auth tokens without egressing traffic to public internet.
- Trade-offs: more operational overhead, longer lead time for setup, but highest isolation guarantees for regulated data.

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll send network_boundary_diagram.png and an ops checklist showing the ALB and security group changes.
2) Marissa will draft a sample contract clause specifying the retention window you prefer (90 days) and the purge API conditions.
3) If you want confirmation, we can spin a short Private VPC PoC environment (2 GPUs) to validate connectivity.

Please confirm which items you want prioritized. If you want the PoC, what's your desired start date?

Best,
Rafael
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Lucy,

Adding a few implementation-level notes and the attachment I promised: network_boundary_diagram.png (see attachments). A couple of clarifying points based on your compliance checklist: 

- KMS/HSM: For Private VPC we support BYOK via customer KMS; keys never leave your control plane. For Dedicated we can integrate with customer KMS for disk encryption but key material is managed by Redwood's HSM unless a contractual BYOK addon is requested.
- Audit logs: In Dedicated we stream audit logs to a customer-owned S3 (recommended) or keep them in Redwood for 90 days by default. For Private VPC audit logs are owner-managed and retained per your policy.
- Network ACLs: The ALB must allow the Redwood inference node IP range (I'll provide the CIDR block in a separate secure doc).

I've also started drafting the 90-day retention clause for legal. Rafael — can you add the SLA numbers for tail latency and throughput for the 2xA100 PoC so Lucy's ops team can size it?

Thanks,
Marissa
